description: Montana-only rules checked against the Montana Code Annotated 2025. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: On a Montana interstate highway outside an urbanized area of 50,000 population or more, the speed limit is
options: 70 mph in daytime and 65 mph at night
80 miles an hour at all times
questions.explanation: Section 61-8-303(1)(a) sets 80 miles an hour at all times on an interstate highway outside an urbanized area of 50,000 or more, and 65 miles an hour at all times on interstate highways within such an urbanized area. Those limits may be altered as authorized in the sections named in subsection (6).

questions.q: Inside a Montana urban district, unless a lawful alteration applies, the speed limit is
questions.explanation: Section 61-8-303(1)(d) sets 25 miles an hour in an urban district. A local authority may alter limits under 61-8-310, including a school-zone decrease, but that section does not itself set the school-zone speed at 15; it says a decrease may not go below 15 miles an hour.

questions.q: On any other Montana public highway, the statutory limits are
questions.explanation: Section 61-8-303(1)(c) sets 70 miles an hour during the daytime and 65 miles an hour during the nighttime on any other public highway. Subsection (5) defines daytime as from one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset, and nighttime as any other hour.

questions.q: A Montana driver on a two-lane road in a designated passing zone may exceed the 61-8-303 limit
options: By 10 mph to pass and safely return to the right lane
By 15 mph if the vehicle being passed is a truck
questions.explanation: Section 61-8-303(2) allows a vehicle to exceed the subsection (1) limits by 10 miles an hour to overtake and pass and return safely to the right-hand lane only while traveling on a two-lane road and in a designated passing zone.

questions.q: Montana's per se driving-under-the-influence rule for a noncommercial vehicle is an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 61-8-1002(1)(b) says a person commits driving under the influence by driving or being in actual physical control of a noncommercial vehicle on ways open to the public while the person's alcohol concentration is 0.08 or more.

questions.q: For a commercial motor vehicle in Montana, driving under the influence includes an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 61-8-1002(1)(c) applies when a person drives or is in actual physical control of a commercial motor vehicle within the state while the person's alcohol concentration is 0.04 or more.

questions.q: A Montana driver under 21 commits driving under the influence at an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 61-8-1002(1)(e)(i) covers a person under 21 years of age at the time of the offense who drives a vehicle while the person's alcohol concentration is 0.02 or more.

questions.q: Montana's statutory point schedule is used to identify a habitual traffic offender. That status requires
questions.explanation: Section 61-11-203(1)(b) defines a habitual traffic offender as any person who within a 3-year period accumulates 30 or more conviction points under the schedule in subsection (2). Montana does not use that schedule as a 12-point suspension system.

questions.q: On Montana's habitual-offender point schedule, driving while under the influence is
questions.explanation: Section 61-11-203(2)(d) assigns 10 points for driving while under the influence of intoxicating liquor or narcotics or drugs of any kind. Reckless driving is 5 points under subsection (2)(h).

questions.q: Montana assigns how many habitual-offender points for speeding, except as provided in 61-8-725(2)(a)?
questions.explanation: Section 61-11-203(2)(l) assigns 3 points for speeding, except as provided in 61-8-725(2)(a). All other moving violations are 2 points under subsection (2)(m).

questions.q: If one Montana incident produces two or more convictions, the habitual-offender count uses
options: The sum of every conviction's points
Only the conviction that carries the highest points
An average of the point values
No points, because only one ticket was written
questions.explanation: Section 61-11-203(3) says if there are two or more convictions involving a single occurrence, only the number of points for the specific conviction carrying the highest points is chargeable against that defendant.

questions.q: For the first 6 months of Montana's 1-year minor restriction, passengers under 18 are limited to
options: One, unless supervised or the others are family
Three, the same limit used for the whole year
Any number if they wear seat belts
questions.explanation: Section 61-5-133(1)(c)(i) says that for the first 6 months a restricted licensee may not operate with more than one passenger under 18 unless supervised by a licensed driver at least 18 or the additional passengers under 18 are family. For the second 6 months the limit is three, with the same exceptions.

questions.q: In Montana, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Montana issues a learner's permit for a car at 14½ years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Montana car permit: 14½ years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: Drivers Under 18 – MT Motor Vehicle Division

questions.q: In Montana, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Montana requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: 61-5-132. Prerequisites for issuance of driver's license to minor, MCA

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Montana complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Montana requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: 61-5-132. Prerequisites for issuance of driver's license to minor, MCA

questions.q: Of a Montana teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Montana requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Montana: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: 61-5-132. Prerequisites for issuance of driver's license to minor, MCA

questions.q: In Montana, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Montana, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 15 years.

provenance.manual: Drivers Under 18 – MT Motor Vehicle Division

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Montana not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Montana restricts provisional drivers from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: Montana new drivers: off the road 11 p.m. to 5 a.m..

provenance.manual: 61-5-133. First year restrictions on driver's license issued to minor, MCA

questions.q: In Montana, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Montana drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Drivers Under 18 – MT Motor Vehicle Division

questions.q: In Montana, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Montana, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Montana, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

questions.q: In Montana, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Montana brings a suspension of 180 days.
questions.remember: Montana, first refusal: 180 days without a license.

provenance.manual: 61-8-1032. Mandatory suspension of license following certain implied consent action, MCA

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Montana?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Montana can be posted up to 80 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Montana rural interstate: up to 80 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Montana's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Montana: no statewide ban on phone use or texting.
questions.remember: Montana phone law: no statewide ban.

questions.q: How is Montana's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Montana seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Montana?
questions.explanation: Montana requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Montana: car or booster seat until 8 years.

provenance.manual: 61-9-420. Child safety restraint systems -- standards -- exemptions, MCA

questions.q: What is Montana's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Montana requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $20,000.

provenance.manual: 61-6-103. Motor vehicle liability policy minimum limits -- other requirements, MCA

questions.q: Under Montana's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Montana can suspend an adult's license at 30 points in 36 months.

provenance.manual: 61-11-203. Definitions -- habitual traffic offenders -- point schedule, MCA
